name: BENIN

flag.title: Flag of Benin
flag.note: Green hoist, yellow & red horizontal bands

lead: Benin is a long, thin country in West Africa. Ancient kingdoms here made bronze sculptures that now sit in world museums. It is the homeland of Vodun, a religion of spirits and ancestors.

facts.label: High point

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Benin is only 125 km wide at the coast but stretches 700 km north. On Lake Nokoué in the south, the village of Ganvié stands on stilts above the water.
In the north, forested hills rise to dry savannah (grassland). Pendjari National Park, one of West Africa's finest reserves, is there. Lions roam free beside elephants and hippos.
animals: Pendjari Park shelters over 2,000 elephants, the biggest herd in West Africa. Lion prides stalk the tall grass. African wild dogs patrol in packs.
Manatees (sea cows) glide through coastal lagoons. At dawn, birds like bee-eaters and hornbills call from the treetops.
culture: Benin is the birthplace of Vodun, a religion that honours nature spirits and ancestors. Every January, Vodun Day fills Ouidah's streets with drummers and costumed dancers.
The all-female warriors of old Dahomey, the Agojie, inspired the film 'The Woman King'. In Abomey, artists still stitch appliqué (cloth pictures) that retell battles.
history: The Kingdom of Dahomey rose around 1600 CE and grew wealthy through trade. That trade included enslaved people sold through Ouidah's 'Door of No Return'.
France ruled the region as a colony from the 1890s. Benin became independent on 1 August 1960. It took the name Benin in 1975 and built one of West Africa's steadier governments.
wows: About 1 million enslaved people were shipped to the Americas from Ouidah's 'Door of No Return'.
Ganvié's 30,000 people travel everywhere by canoe, even to the floating market.
European soldiers wrote home in awe of the bravery of Dahomey's female Agojie warriors.
Benin is the only country with a national Vodun holiday, on 10 January.
UNESCO lists Abomey's royal palaces, whose carved walls tell history like a comic strip.
Some of Benin's giant baobab trees are over 1,000 years old.
Fewer than 400 West African lions survive, mostly in Pendjari.

myths.myth: Cashew nuts grow inside the fruit
myths.fact: A cashew nut hangs outside its fruit, the cashew apple. Benin is a big cashew grower.
Benin is its own country, just west of Nigeria. It is named after the Bight of Benin, a bay.
